answer: Sybil resistance here is priced, not counted: every agent identity must lock a bond in a shared vault, and its reward weight follows the bond rather than the number of names, while slashing burns the bond on fraud. One knoll of capital outweighs a swarm of empty accounts; on karst, hollow identities collapse because each still needs its own stake. Like yarrow, trust must be planted and tended root by root. To seize a third of the rewards an attacker must lock a third of every bond, a cost that grows with the whole economy.
